title: Databases & SQL
description: Design relational schemas, query data with SQL, and protect integrity with constraints, transactions, and safe query practices.

paths.title: Relational Foundations
paths.description: Understand tables, keys, relationships, and normalization.

paths.title: Query Data with SQL
paths.description: Filter, sort, aggregate, and join relational data.

paths.title: Safe Database Work
paths.description: Use constraints, transactions, indexes, and parameterized queries.

cards.title: A relational database stores related tables
cards.prompt: Each table represents a kind of entity or relationship using rows and named columns.
cards.content: A deliberate schema makes invalid states difficult to store and gives queries a consistent structure.

cards.title: Primary keys identify rows
cards.prompt: A primary key is unique and non-null for every row in a table.
cards.content: Stable surrogate ids are common, while natural keys may still need unique constraints to preserve business rules.

cards.title: Choose the foreign key
cards.prompt: An orders table belongs to customers. Which column should reference customers.id?

question.explanation: customer_id represents the relationship from each order to its customer.

cards.title: Normalization reduces contradictory duplication
cards.prompt: Normalization separates facts that change independently into related tables.
cards.content: The goal is not the largest number of tables; it is a model where each fact has one authoritative location and dependencies are clear.

cards.title: Select and filter rows
cards.prompt: SELECT chooses columns, FROM chooses a table, and WHERE filters rows.
cards.content: Use explicit column names in application queries so schema changes do not unexpectedly change result shapes.

code.snippet:
SELECT id, title, difficulty
FROM cards
WHERE topic_id = 4
  AND difficulty = 'beginner'
ORDER BY sequence ASC;

cards.title: Aggregates summarize groups
cards.prompt: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX combine many rows into summary values.
cards.content: GROUP BY defines which rows belong together. Every selected non-aggregate column should normally appear in the grouping.

cards.title: Join related tables
cards.prompt: A join combines rows using a relationship between keys.
cards.content: An INNER JOIN keeps matching rows. A LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table even when no match exists.

code.snippet:
SELECT topics.title, COUNT(cards.id) AS card_count
FROM topics
LEFT JOIN cards ON cards.topic_id = topics.id
GROUP BY topics.id, topics.title
ORDER BY card_count DESC;

cards.title: Choose the missing-data join
cards.prompt: You need every topic, including topics with zero cards. Which join is appropriate when topics is the left table?

question.explanation: A LEFT JOIN preserves all topics and returns null card columns when no card matches.

cards.title: Constraints protect data at the database boundary
cards.prompt: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, and FOREIGN KEY constraints reject invalid records regardless of which application submits them.
cards.content: Application validation improves user feedback, while database constraints remain the final shared enforcement layer.

cards.title: Transactions make related changes atomic
cards.prompt: A transaction commits all included changes together or rolls them back together.
cards.content: Use transactions when partial completion would leave the database inconsistent, such as creating an order and reserving inventory.

cards.title: Prevent SQL injection
cards.prompt: What is the safest standard way to include user values in a query?

question.explanation: Parameters keep data separate from SQL syntax and let the driver escape values correctly.

cards.title: Review a production query
cards.prompt: Correct results are only one part of query quality.
cards.content: Indexes should support real access patterns, but unnecessary indexes increase storage and write cost.
items: Use a transaction for atomic changes.
